description:
FOUND s506f (Opus, 2026-10-04) building -F (perl quotes a plain -F pattern as the STRING q\0PAT\0,
which split compiles as a pattern).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL 618db500):
  pcl  -e 'my @F = split(q{x+}, "axxb"); print "[$F[1]]\n"'   -> []      perl: [b]
  pcl  -e 'my @F = split(q{\.}, "a.b");  print "[$F[1]]\n"'   -> []      perl: [b]
  pcl  -e 'my $p = q{\.}; my @F = split($p, "a.b"); print "[$F[1]]\n"' -> []  perl: [b]
  perl -e 'print scalar(my @x = split("|", "abc")), "\n"'     -> 3 (an empty alternation splits every char)

CAUSE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp p-split's last cond arm ";; Literal string pattern" uses SEARCH on the
string; only a p-regex-match object reaches cl-ppcre.  perl (pp_split) compiles any non-regex EXPR
as a pattern, except the single-space string ' ' (awk mode, already handled).  A pattern string
WITHOUT metacharacters (`split(',', $s)`, the common case) gives the same answer either way, which is
why this survived.

WORKAROUND in s506f: PCLSwitches emits a plain -F pattern as `split(m'PAT')`, so -F is right
regardless.  FIX: route the string through the same scanner path (cache the compiled scanner per
string); probe `split('.', $s)`, `split('|', $s)`, `split('^', $s)` (perl: /^/m), `split(' ', ...)`
stays awk mode, `split(q{ }, ...)` too.  cl/ change: sweep + op/split.t companion.
subject: split with a STRING pattern (`split('x+', $s)`, `split($p, $s)`, `split('|', $s)`) splits on the LITERAL text; perl compiles the string as a regex
